Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1) demonstrates hyperinflation of the left lung with increased radiolucency and flattening of the left hemidiaphragm, accompanied by a shift of the mediastinum to the right. This finding, combined with the clinical history of sudden dyspnea and recurrent cough in an infant, is characteristic of a ball-valve obstruction (often by a mass or foreign body) causing air trapping on the affected side, which pushes the mediastinum to the contralateral side.
